notes.definition: A specialised cell has a structure and sub-cellular features that adapt it to carry out a particular function. Examples are sperm cells, nerve cells and muscle cells in animals, and root hair, xylem and phloem cells in plants.
explanation: In a multicellular organism, cells do not all do the same job. Many cells are specialised: their shape, size and sub-cellular structures are adapted to carry out a particular function. Specialised cells work together in tissues, tissues make up organs and organs make up organ systems. When you explain an adaptation, always link the feature to the function: say what the feature is and how it helps the cell, tissue, organ or whole organism.

A sperm cell carries the male's genetic information to the egg. It has a long tail that whips from side to side so it can swim. Its mid-piece is packed with mitochondria, which carry out aerobic respiration to release the energy the tail needs. The acrosome at the tip of the head stores digestive enzymes that break down the outer layers of the egg, and the large nucleus contains half the genetic information of a normal body cell. The head is streamlined to help it move.

Nerve cells carry electrical impulses around the body. They are long, so impulses can be carried over long distances, for example from the spinal cord to the foot. They have branched endings (dendrites) so they can connect with many other nerve cells. Muscle cells contract to move the body. They contain special proteins that slide over each other, making the fibres shorter. They contain many mitochondria to release the energy needed for contraction, and can store glycogen, which can be broken down to glucose for respiration.

Root hair cells absorb water and mineral ions from the soil. The long root hair gives a large surface area, which increases the rate of absorption. They have many mitochondria to release energy for the active transport of mineral ions, and a large permanent vacuole that helps water move in by osmosis. They have no chloroplasts because they grow underground where there is no light.

Xylem cells carry water and dissolved mineral ions from the roots to the rest of the plant. They are dead cells joined end to end with no end walls, forming long hollow tubes so water can flow through without obstruction. Their walls are strengthened by spirals or rings of lignin, which helps them withstand the pressure of water and supports the plant. Phloem cells carry dissolved sugars up and down the plant. Phloem is made of elongated sieve tube cells whose end walls have pores (sieve plates), so cell sap can move from one cell to the next. Sieve tube cells have lost most sub-cellular structures, and companion cells next to them contain many mitochondria to release the energy needed.
keyFacts: Specialised cells have features that adapt them to a particular function.
Sperm cell: tail to swim, many mitochondria in the mid-piece, acrosome containing enzymes, nucleus with half the genetic information.
Nerve cell: long to carry impulses over long distances, branched endings to connect to many other cells.
Muscle cell: proteins that slide over each other to contract, many mitochondria, stores glycogen.
Root hair cell: large surface area, many mitochondria for active transport, no chloroplasts, large permanent vacuole.
Xylem: dead cells, no end walls, hollow tubes, walls strengthened by lignin, carry water and mineral ions upwards.
Phloem: sieve tubes with sieve plates (pores in end walls), few sub-cellular structures, companion cells with many mitochondria, carry dissolved sugars up and down.
Always link each feature to how it helps the cell carry out its function.

keyTerms.definition: A cell that has a structure and sub-cellular features adapted to carry out a particular function.
A feature that helps a cell (or organism) carry out its function or survive in its environment.
A structure at the tip of a sperm cell's head that contains enzymes to digest a way through the outer layers of the egg.
A tough substance that strengthens the walls of xylem cells.
An end wall between phloem sieve tube cells that has pores so cell sap containing sugars can pass through.
A cell next to a phloem sieve tube that contains many mitochondria and supplies the energy the sieve tube needs.
A long, thin extension of a root epidermis cell that gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions.
A storage carbohydrate in animal cells such as muscle cells that can be broken down to glucose for respiration.

workedExamples.title: Explaining an adaptation (feature plus function)
workedExamples.question: Explain how one feature of a sperm cell helps it to fertilise an egg.
steps: Pick a feature: the mid-piece contains many mitochondria.
Say what the feature does: mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, releasing energy.
Link it to the function: the energy is used by the tail to swim to the egg.
workedExamples.answer: The mid-piece has many mitochondria, which release energy by aerobic respiration so the tail can move and the sperm can swim to the egg.

workedExamples.title: Using unfamiliar information
workedExamples.question: Cells lining the small intestine have tiny folds in their membranes called microvilli. Suggest how this helps the cells absorb digested food.
steps: Identify the effect of the feature: folds increase the surface area of the cell membrane.
Link to function: a larger surface area means more food molecules can be absorbed at the same time.
Compare with a known example: this is the same idea as a root hair cell having a large surface area to absorb water.
workedExamples.answer: Microvilli increase the surface area of the membrane, so the rate of absorption of digested food is increased.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think root hair cells photosynthesise because they are plant cells.
misconceptions.right: In fact root hair cells have no chloroplasts. They are underground, where there is no light, so they cannot photosynthesise.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think xylem and phloem both carry water.
misconceptions.right: In fact xylem carries water and mineral ions up from the roots, while phloem carries dissolved sugars both up and down the plant.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think xylem cells are living cells full of cytoplasm.
misconceptions.right: In fact mature xylem cells are dead. They have no cytoplasm and no end walls, so they form hollow tubes for water to flow through.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often write that mitochondria in sperm cells 'make energy'.
misconceptions.right: In fact mitochondria release energy by aerobic respiration. Energy is never made.

realWorld: Some forms of male infertility are caused by sperm with poorly working mitochondria or tails, so the sperm cannot swim well enough to reach the egg.
Damage to the long nerve cells in the spinal cord can cause paralysis because impulses can no longer travel between the brain and the muscles.
Gardeners water and feed plants at the roots because root hair cells are where water and mineral ions are absorbed; damaging roots when transplanting causes plants to wilt.
examTips: For 'explain how this cell is adapted' questions, use a two-part answer for every feature: the feature, then 'so that' or 'which allows' plus its function.
Name the process when you mention mitochondria: 'many mitochondria to release energy by respiration for active transport' scores better than 'lots of mitochondria for energy'.
Learn which way substances move: xylem is one way (up) for water and mineral ions; phloem is both ways for dissolved sugars.
In questions about an unfamiliar cell, use what you know: folds or projections increase surface area, many mitochondria mean lots of energy is needed, many ribosomes mean lots of protein is made.
Do not say root hair cells absorb 'nutrients' or 'food'. Say water (by osmosis) and mineral ions (by active transport).
summary: Specialised cells are adapted for a particular function.
Animal examples: sperm cells, nerve cells, muscle cells.
Plant examples: root hair cells, xylem cells, phloem cells.
Large surface area increases absorption; many mitochondria release lots of energy.
Xylem: dead, hollow, lignified tubes carrying water and mineral ions upwards.
Phloem: sieve tubes with sieve plates and companion cells carrying dissolved sugars up and down.

flashcards.back: A cell with features that adapt it to carry out a particular function.

flashcards.front: Why does a sperm cell have many mitochondria?
flashcards.back: To release energy by aerobic respiration so the tail can move and the sperm can swim.

flashcards.front: What is the acrosome of a sperm cell for?
flashcards.back: It contains enzymes that digest a way through the outer layers of the egg.
To carry electrical impulses over long distances around the body.

flashcards.front: Why do nerve cells have branched endings?
flashcards.back: To connect with many other nerve cells.
Special proteins slide over each other, making the fibres shorter.

flashcards.front: Why do muscle cells have many mitochondria?
flashcards.back: To release the energy needed for contraction.

flashcards.front: Give two adaptations of a root hair cell.
flashcards.back: Large surface area (root hair); many mitochondria for active transport; large permanent vacuole; no chloroplasts.
Water and dissolved mineral ions, upwards from the roots.
Dissolved sugars, both up and down the plant.
End walls in phloem sieve tubes with pores so cell sap can flow from cell to cell.

flashcards.front: Why do companion cells have many mitochondria?
flashcards.back: To release the energy needed by the phloem sieve tube cells, which have few sub-cellular structures.

questions.question: Which specialised cell has a tail so that it can swim?
markScheme: 1 mark: sperm cell
questions.explanation: Sperm cells use their tail to swim towards the egg. Nerve cells have long extensions but do not swim, and root hairs are fixed in the soil.

questions.question: What is the main function of a root hair cell?
options: To absorb water and mineral ions from the soil
markScheme: 1 mark: to absorb water and mineral ions from the soil
questions.explanation: Root hair cells absorb water and mineral ions. They cannot photosynthesise because they have no chloroplasts. Phloem transports sugars and nerve cells carry impulses.

questions.question: Which type of cell carries electrical impulses around the body?
markScheme: 1 mark: nerve cell
questions.explanation: Nerve cells (neurones) carry electrical impulses. Muscle cells respond to impulses by contracting, but they do not carry them around the body.

questions.question: Which plant tissue transports water from the roots to the leaves?
markScheme: 1 mark: xylem
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and mineral ions up the plant. Phloem carries dissolved sugars. Muscle is an animal tissue.

questions.question: Why does the mid-piece of a sperm cell contain many mitochondria?
options: To digest the outer layer of the egg
To make proteins for the egg
To release energy by respiration so the tail can move
markScheme: 1 mark: to release energy by respiration so the tail can move
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, which releases energy for swimming. Enzymes in the acrosome digest the egg's outer layer, and genetic information is in the nucleus.

questions.question: What does the acrosome of a sperm cell contain?
options: Enzymes that digest a way into the egg
markScheme: 1 mark: enzymes that digest a way into the egg
questions.explanation: The acrosome is a sac of digestive enzymes at the tip of the head. The mitochondria are in the mid-piece and the genetic information is in the nucleus.

questions.question: Which substance strengthens the walls of xylem cells?
markScheme: 1 mark: lignin
questions.explanation: Rings or spirals of lignin strengthen xylem walls so the tubes do not collapse and help support the plant. Glycogen is an animal storage carbohydrate and chlorophyll is found in chloroplasts.

questions.question: How do muscle cells contract?
options: Special proteins slide over each other, making the fibres shorter
markScheme: 1 mark: special proteins slide over each other, making the fibres shorter
questions.explanation: Muscle cells contain protein filaments that slide over each other, shortening the cell. Animal cells have no cell walls, and contraction has nothing to do with absorbing water or cell division.

questions.question: Mature xylem cells have no end walls and no cytoplasm. What is the advantage of this?
options: Water can flow through a continuous hollow tube without obstruction
Sugars can be moved by active transport
markScheme: 1 mark: water can flow through a continuous hollow tube without obstruction
questions.explanation: With no end walls or cell contents in the way, xylem forms open tubes for water. Dead xylem cells cannot photosynthesise or divide, and sugars are carried in phloem, not xylem.

questions.question: Phloem sieve tube cells have very few sub-cellular structures. Companion cells next to them contain many mitochondria. What is the best explanation for this?
options: Companion cells photosynthesise to make sugar for the sieve tubes
Companion cells carry water up the plant
Mitochondria in companion cells make dissolved sugars
Companion cells release the energy needed to move dissolved sugars in the sieve tubes
markScheme: 1 mark: companion cells release the energy needed to move dissolved sugars in the sieve tubes
questions.explanation: Sieve tubes lack most sub-cellular structures so that sap can flow easily, so companion cells supply energy from respiration in their mitochondria. Mitochondria do not make sugars, and water moves in xylem.

questions.question: State the function of phloem tissue.
markScheme: 1 mark: transports dissolved sugars (around the plant)
questions.explanation: Phloem carries dissolved sugars made in the leaves to other parts of the plant, both up and down.

questions.question: Name the type of specialised animal cell that contracts to move parts of the body.
markScheme: 1 mark: muscle cell
questions.explanation: Muscle cells contract, using protein fibres that slide over each other, to move bones and organs.

questions.question: Give two ways a root hair cell is adapted to its function.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two from: long root hair / large surface area; many mitochondria (for active transport); large permanent vacuole (helps osmosis); thin cell wall
questions.explanation: The root hair increases surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions. Mitochondria release energy for active transport of mineral ions. The permanent vacuole helps water move in by osmosis.

questions.question: Explain why root hair cells do not have chloroplasts.
markScheme: 1 mark: they are underground / receive no light
1 mark: so they cannot photosynthesise / chloroplasts would have no use
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are used for photosynthesis, which needs light. Root hair cells are in the soil, so chloroplasts would be no use to them.

questions.question: Explain how being long helps a nerve cell carry out its function.
acceptedAnswers: connect distant parts of the body
markScheme: 1 mark: nerve cells carry electrical impulses
1 mark: being long means impulses can be carried over long distances (e.g. from the spinal cord to the foot)
questions.explanation: A single long nerve cell can carry an impulse a long way, linking distant parts of the body, such as the spinal cord and muscles in the foot.

questions.question: Root hair cells contain many mitochondria. Explain why.
markScheme: 1 mark: mitochondria release energy by (aerobic) respiration
1 mark: energy is needed for the active transport of mineral ions into the cell
questions.explanation: Mineral ions are taken up against a concentration gradient by active transport, which needs energy. Mitochondria release this energy through aerobic respiration.

questions.question: Nerve cells have many branched endings. Describe how this helps them carry out their function.
acceptedAnswers: connect with many other nerve cells
markScheme: 1 mark: branched endings connect with many other (nerve) cells
1 mark: so impulses can be passed to / received from many cells
questions.explanation: The branched endings let one nerve cell link with many others, so impulses can travel to or from lots of cells and form networks.

questions.question: A man has sperm cells whose mitochondria do not work properly. Suggest and explain how this could affect his chances of fathering a child.
markScheme: 1 mark: less (aerobic) respiration so less energy released
1 mark: tail cannot move / sperm cannot swim well
1 mark: sperm less likely to reach / fertilise the egg, so lower chance of fathering a child
questions.explanation: The mid-piece mitochondria release energy for the tail. Without it, sperm swim poorly and fewer reach the egg, so fertilisation is less likely.

questions.question: Mature xylem cells are dead. Explain why this is an advantage for the transport of water.
markScheme: 1 mark: dead cells have no cytoplasm / sub-cellular structures
1 mark: end walls have broken down
1 mark: forming a hollow continuous tube so water flows without obstruction
questions.explanation: Because the cells are dead, their contents and end walls are gone, leaving open tubes. Water and mineral ions can flow freely from roots to leaves. Lignin keeps these empty tubes from collapsing.

questions.question: Name the plant tissue made of dead cells that form long hollow tubes strengthened by lignin.
markScheme: 1 mark: xylem
questions.explanation: Xylem is made of dead cells with no end walls, strengthened by lignin. Phloem is made of living cells.

questions.question: Muscle cells can store glycogen. Suggest why this is useful to a muscle cell.
markScheme: 1 mark: glycogen can be broken down to glucose
1 mark: glucose is used in respiration to release energy for contraction
questions.explanation: Glycogen is a store of glucose. During exercise it is broken down to glucose, which is used in respiration to release the energy muscles need to contract.

questions.question: Explain how xylem and phloem cells are adapted for transport in a plant.
markScheme: Indicative content:
xylem transports water and mineral ions upwards from the roots
xylem cells are dead / have no cytoplasm
xylem cells have no end walls, forming continuous hollow tubes
so water flows without obstruction
xylem walls are strengthened by lignin so tubes do not collapse / support the plant
phloem transports dissolved sugars up and down the plant
phloem is made of elongated sieve tube cells joined end to end
end walls have pores (sieve plates) so cell sap can flow from cell to cell
sieve tube cells have few sub-cellular structures so sap flows easily
companion cells have many mitochondria to release energy for the sieve tube cells
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): adaptations of both xylem and phloem described and clearly linked to their functions.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): several adaptations described, with some links to function, may focus on one tissue.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements of features or functions with little explanation.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: The best answers deal with both tissues and link each feature to the job: no end walls for free flow and lignin for strength in xylem; sieve plates, few organelles and companion cells with mitochondria in phloem.

questions.question: Describe how a sperm cell is adapted to its function.
markScheme: Indicative content:
function is to reach and fertilise an egg / carry the male genetic information
tail to swim (to the egg)
mid-piece with many mitochondria to release energy for swimming
acrosome containing enzymes to digest through the outer layers of the egg
nucleus containing half the genetic information
streamlined head
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): at least three features each linked to their function.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): features listed with little or no link to function.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Each feature needs a matching function: tail for swimming, mitochondria for energy, acrosome enzymes to get into the egg, and a nucleus with half the genetic information to combine with the egg's.

questions.question: Explain how a root hair cell is adapted to absorb water and mineral ions from the soil.
markScheme: Indicative content:
long root hair gives a large surface area
so the rate of absorption of water and mineral ions is increased
many mitochondria release energy by respiration
energy is used for active transport of mineral ions
large permanent vacuole helps water move in by osmosis
no chloroplasts since no light underground
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): at least two adaptations clearly explained in terms of absorption.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): adaptations named but not explained.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Surface area and mitochondria are the two key adaptations. A large surface area increases absorption, and mitochondria release energy for active transport of mineral ions.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a specialised cell?
options: A cell that can become any type of cell
A cell that has no nucleus
A cell with features that help it carry out a particular function
A cell that only carries out respiration
markScheme: 1 mark: a cell with features that help it carry out a particular function
questions.explanation: Specialised cells have structures adapted for one job. A cell that can become any type of cell is an unspecialised stem cell, which is the opposite.

questions.question: What is transported by phloem?
markScheme: 1 mark: dissolved sugars
questions.explanation: Phloem carries dissolved sugars from the leaves to other parts of the plant. Water and mineral ions travel in the xylem, and carbon dioxide enters leaves by diffusion through stomata.

questions.question: Which row correctly matches a cell, one of its features and the function of that feature?
options: Root hair cell: large surface area: absorbs dissolved sugars from the soil
Xylem cell: sieve plates: let water pass from cell to cell
Sperm cell: acrosome: contains enzymes to digest a way into the egg
Phloem cell: lignin rings: strengthen the cell for carrying mineral ions
markScheme: 1 mark: sperm cell: acrosome: contains enzymes to digest a way into the egg
questions.explanation: Only the sperm row is fully correct. Root hairs absorb water and mineral ions, not sugars. Sieve plates belong to phloem, and lignin rings belong to xylem.

questions.question: Compare what is transported in xylem and in phloem, and the direction of movement in each.
markScheme: 1 mark: xylem carries water and mineral ions, upwards (from roots to leaves)
1 mark: phloem carries dissolved sugars, both up and down
questions.explanation: Xylem flow is one way, up from the roots. Phloem moves sugars from where they are made to where they are used or stored, which can be up or down.
